summary: The required public-repo-history check uses the trusted base's scanner to check every introduced commit, including merge commits and merged side histories, without executing candidate code. A lightweight content-only pre-push guard blocks dirty history before the existing evidence-signing path. Cleaning the final tree no longer hides dirty intermediate commits; evidence signing and the separate landing-signing transition are unchanged.

replay.detail: No runtime replay or stored data change. The guard reads Git commit history.

schema.detail: No database, wire or checkpoint schema change.

rules.detail: No runtime admission or checkpoint rule change. Repository protection requires the public-repo-history context from GitHub Actions integration 15368 in main ruleset 20563764; this change does not mutate live settings.

compatibility.detail: Every commit in merge-base(BASE, HEAD)..HEAD must pass message, path and per-parent added-content checks, including merges. A dirty intermediate commit fails even after a cleanup commit makes the head clean. ST_SKIP_EVIDENCE and ST_EVIDENCE_LOCAL affect only evidence signing, never the content guard. Existing signing behavior is unchanged.

downtime.detail: No service interruption or runtime deployment is required.

manual.detail: Install the repository hooks with scripts/install-git-hooks. If introduced history is dirty, create a replacement branch from a clean base with only public-clean changes and messages, then open a replacement PR. Do not force-push or rebase the existing PR to conceal dirty history.

recovery.detail: A clean head does not repair dirty history. Replace the branch and PR from a clean base rather than adding another cleanup commit or rewriting the existing PR. Bypassing the local hook does not bypass the hosted required check.
